title: the_exact_change
beats: My boss docked my pay eleven minutes for being late. Once. In three years.
Company policy, he said. We track to the minute, he said. It's just fairness, he said.
Cool. Fairness. I can work with fairness.
So I started tracking to the minute too.
Every 6:52 arrival for a 7:00 shift. Logged.
Every lunch I worked through because quote, it's crunch time. Logged.
Every 'can you stay five more minutes' that turned into forty. Logged, dated, and witnessed by two coworkers.
I kept it up for six weeks. Then I ran the numbers.
Nineteen hours and twelve minutes of unpaid, documented time.
I printed the spreadsheet. Three copies. One for him, one for HR, and one for the labor board. I mentioned that last part out loud.
He laughed at the spreadsheet. HR did not laugh at the spreadsheet.
Turns out 'we track to the minute' is a legally binding attitude. Their lawyer used the word 'exposure' four times in one meeting.
I got a check for four hundred dollars and change. Backdated. With interest.
The minute-tracking policy quietly vanished the next quarter.
But every time I walk in at 6:59, he checks his watch. And says nothing.
